Ankit Agrawal vs State Of Punjab on 12 July, 2024 
Author: Kirti Singh
Bench: Kirti Singh
 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:090903
Crm-M-14012-2024 (O&M) 1
 In The High Court Of Punjab & Haryana At
 Chandigarh
 Crm-M-14012-2024 (O&M)
 Reserved on : 12.07.2024
 Pronounced on: 19.07.2024
Ankit Agrawal
 ..... Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Punjab .... Respondent
Coram: Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Kirti Singh 
Present: Mr. Viraj Gandhi, Advocate for the petitioner. 
 Mr. Vinay Kumar, Dag, Punjab. 
 *****
Kirti Singh, J. 
The present petition has been filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail to the
petitioner in Fir No.81 dated 05.12.2023, under Sections 22 and 29 of Narcotic Drugs and
Psychotropic Substances Act 1985, registered at Police Station Banga, District Sbs Nagar, Punjab. 
2.  The brief facts of the case are that allegedly on 05.12.2023 on Phagwara road, Banga, one person namely Dalip Kumar @ Deep was apprehended with conscious possession of 270 loose intoxicating tablets of light orange colour without any label. Thereafter, said Dalip Kumar nominated co-accused Sukhwinder Singh @ Binda and during investigation Sukhwinder Singh @ Binda nominated the petitioner in his disclosure statement. 
Ankit Agrawal vs State Of Punjab on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89814337/
1 1 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:090903 Subsequently, 50 boxes each containing 10x6x10 strips totalling 30,000 tablets of Alprazolam were recovered from the possession of the petitioner from his premise i.e. a medical shop in Shikohabad, Firozabad, Uttar Pradesh. 
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner inter alia submits that the petitioner was arrested from the premises of the medical store in Uttar Pradesh of which he is an authorized signatory since 23.04.2021. He further submits that medical store namely M/s Agrawal Medical Store is the duly licensed seller and distributor of the Alprazolam drug which was seized by the Investigating Agency. 
The license has been issued by the Food and Safety Drug Administration, an authority under the Government of Uttar Pradesh, under Form 20-B and Form 21-B to the aforesaid firm, which is valid till 31.12.2027. The copies of the licenses and other documents including GST registrations, bills etc.
are annexed as Annexure P-3. Reference is also made to the order dated 01.07.2024, whereby co-accused has been granted the concession of regular bail by this Court in CRM-M- 10951-2024.
4. It is also argued that the petitioner was not named in the FIR and has been entangled only by virtue of involving Section 29 of the NDPS Act by relying upon the disclosure statement of the second co-accused- Sukhwinder Singh @ Binda, who was nominated on the disclosure statement of the first co-accused-Dalip Kumar @ Deep.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance upon the judgments rendered in the cases of "Tofan Singh Vs State of Tamil Nadu" (2021) 4 SCC 1, "Surinder Kumar Khanna Vs Intelligence Officer 2 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:090903 Directorate of Revenue Intelligence" (2018) 8 SCC 721, " Sanjeev Chandra Agarwal & Anr Vs Union of India" (2021) 20 SCC 57, wherein, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down certain observations regarding release of accused on bail. He also relied upon the judgments passed by this Court in "Anil Kumar Vs State of Punjab" (CRM-M-32408-2020), Ajaypal Singh alias Ajay Vs State of Punjab"
(CRM-M-30519-2018), "Vipul Goyal Vs State of Haryana" (CRM-M-9492-2021) and "Harjit Singh Vs State of Punjab" (CRM-M-37650-2021). He further placed reliance on the judgment "Love Gupta @ Hemendra Gupta Vs. State of U.P." in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.25338 of 2019 and "Manojbhai madanlal Mahesvari Vs State of Gujarat" 2021 SCC Online Guj 546.
6. Attention has also been drawn to an order dated 15.02.2023 passed by High Court of Uttar Pradesh in Writ-C-3749-2023, whereby the notification/memorandum dated 15.08.2022 issued by Food Safety and Drug Administration, Uttar Pradesh, vide which maximum limit for storage and sale was imposed on licensed drug dealers, was stayed as an interim measure due to alleged want of jurisdiction. 
7. Learned State counsel has filed the custody certificate dated 11.07.2024 in Court today, which is taken on record. As per custody certificate, the petitioner has undergone an actual custody of 06 months and 27 days and there is no other criminal case pending against him. However, the learned State counsel has opposed the bail by submitting that in view of the serious allegations against the petitioner, he is not entitled to the concession of regular bail. 
3 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:090903 Ankit Agrawal vs State Of Punjab on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89814337/
2 8. This Court has considered the rival submissions made by both the parties. 
9. From the perusal of the status report filed by the State, it is apparent that the proprietor of the Firm is Anil Kumar Agarwal, who is the father of the present petitioner. Relevant paragraph No.16 of the status report is reproduced as below:
"16. That it is further submitted that information regarding license No. SKP-3/85-86 and SKP-4/85-86, issue date 25.05.1985, New license No. UP83200000241,
UP8320000239, valid up to 31.12.2027 was sought from Drug Inspector, Firozabad and as per their letter dated 02.05.2024, the said licenses are valid and proprietor of the firm is Shri Anil Kumar Agarwal son of Shri Sham Babu Agarwal, resident of 1916, Katara Bazar, Shikohabad, District Firozabad, Uttar Pradesh. "
10. The veracity of the allegations levelled against the petitioner shall be established during the course of the trial. It is also apparent that the petitioner is the first time offender and he is having a valid license for running the chemist shop. Admittedly, the petitioner is in custody since 14.12.2023 and out of a total of 18 prosecution witnesses, none has been examined till date. There is no other criminal case pending against him. Keeping in view the fact and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that further incarceration of the petitioner would not serve any purpose. 
11. As per the principle of the criminal jurisprudence, no one should be considered guilty till the guilt is proved beyond reasonable doubt. Detaining the petitioner behind bars for an indefinite period would amount to violation of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and is against the principle "Bail is a rule, jail is an exception" as elucidated in the judgement 4 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:090903 of Apex Court in "Dataram Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another;,
(2018) 3 SCC 22". 
12. Without commenting anything on the merits of the case, lest it may prejudice the trial, the present petition is allowed and the petitioner is ordered to be released on regular bail on his furnishing adequate bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of the concerned learned trial Court/Duty Magistrate. The petitioner shall also abide by the following conditions:-
(I) The petitioner will not tamper with the evidence during the trial. (II) The petitioner will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(s). 
(III) The petitioner will appear before the trial Court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted. 
(IV) The petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused of, or for commission of which he is suspected. (V) The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence. 
Ankit Agrawal vs State Of Punjab on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89814337/
3 13. In addition, the petitioner (or anyone on her behalf) shall prepare an FDR in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and deposit the same with the Trial Court. The same would be liable to be forfeited as per law in case of the absence of the petitioner from trial without sufficient cause. 
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move an application for cancellation of bail before this Court. 
 (KIRTI SINGH)
 JUDGE 19.07.2024 Kavita Nain Whether speaking / reasoned Yes /No Whether Reportable Yes/No  5 of 5 Ankit Agrawal vs State Of Punjab on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89814337/
